# convex_deployment (Resource)

Manages a cloud deployment within a Convex project.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "convex_project" "app" {
  team_id = var.convex_team_id
  name    = "My Application"
}

# The project's default production deployment.
resource "convex_deployment" "prod" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "prod"
  region          = "aws-eu-west-1"
  is_default      = true

  # Production defaults to false. Turning it on streams function logs to
  # connected clients, which is useful while debugging but noisy otherwise.
  send_logs_to_client = true
}

# A second prod deployment in the same project. Anything beyond the default
# one needs its own reference.
resource "convex_deployment" "prod_us" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "prod"
  region          = "aws-us-east-1"
  reference       = "prod-us"

  # Skip the dashboard's edit confirmation prompt, which is on by default for
  # production deployments.
  dashboard_edit_confirmation = false
}

# Dev deployments default to sending logs to the client; turn it off
# explicitly rather than by removing the attribute, which would keep whatever
# was last applied.
resource "convex_deployment" "dev" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "dev"
  reference       = "dev-shared"

  send_logs_to_client = false
}

output "prod_url" {
  value = convex_deployment.prod.deployment_url
}

output "prod_name" {
  # Something like "playful-otter-123".
  value = convex_deployment.prod.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `deployment_type` (String) Type of the deployment. One of `dev`, `prod`, `preview` or `custom`. This can be changed in place; when changing the type of a default deployment, set `is_default` explicitly at the same time.
- `project_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the project that owns the deployment. Changing this forces a new deployment.

### Optional

- `class` (String) Deployment class, for example `s16` or `s256`. Defaults to the team's default class. Changing it requires the deployment class selection entitlement.
- `dashboard_edit_confirmation` (Boolean) Whether the dashboard asks for confirmation before allowing edits during a browser session. Defaults to `true` for `prod` deployments and `false` for `dev` and `preview`.

Removing this from configuration keeps the last applied value rather than restoring the default; set it explicitly instead.
- `expires_at` (Number) Timestamp in milliseconds at which Convex deletes this deployment. Must be at least 30 minutes in the future and within the team's preview deployment retention entitlement. Preview deployments get one by default.

Removing this from configuration keeps the last applied value rather than restoring the default; set it explicitly instead.
- `is_default` (Boolean) For a `prod` deployment, whether it is the project's default production deployment (the one `npx convex deploy` uses). For a `dev` deployment, whether it is the default development deployment of the member that created it. Cannot be set on `preview` or `custom` deployments.
- `reference` (String) Identifier that uniquely identifies this deployment within the project. Supplying one lets a project hold several dev or prod deployments. Generated by Convex when not set.

Convex namespaces the reference under the deployment type, so setting `preview-shared` on a `preview` deployment is stored as `preview/preview-shared`. This attribute keeps the value as written; see `qualified_reference` for the stored form.

Must be 3-100 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `/`, must not start with `local-`, and must not be a reserved word. Note one non-obvious rule: a reference may not have the shape of a deployment name (word-word-number), so `prod-eu-2` is rejected while `prod-eu-west-2` is fine. All of this is checked at plan time.
- `region` (String) Hosting region, one of `aws-us-east-1` or `aws-eu-west-1`. Defaults to the team's default region. Convex cannot move a deployment between regions, so changing this forces a new deployment.
- `send_logs_to_client` (Boolean) Whether function logs are sent to the client. Defaults to `true` for `dev` and `preview` deployments and `false` for `prod`.

Removing this from configuration keeps the last applied value rather than restoring the default; set it explicitly instead.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (Number) Creation timestamp, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `creator` (Number) Numeric member ID of whoever created the deployment.
- `deployment_url` (String) Backend URL of the deployment, for example `https://playful-otter-123.convex.cloud`. This is always a `.convex.cloud` URL, even when custom domains are configured.
- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the deployment.
- `last_deploy_time` (Number) Timestamp of the last push to this deployment, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, or null if nothing has been deployed yet. This changes outside Terraform whenever code is deployed.
- `name` (String) Readable identifier assigned by Convex, such as `playful-otter-123`. This is the value the API addresses the deployment by, and the value to use when importing.
- `preview_identifier` (String) Preview identifier, set only on `preview` deployments.
- `qualified_reference` (String) The reference as Convex stores it, namespaced under the deployment type (for example `preview/preview-shared`). Use this when something outside Terraform needs the reference exactly as the API reports it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Deployments are imported by name, not by numeric ID -- the name is what the
# API addresses them by.
terraform import convex_deployment.prod playful-otter-123
```
